transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I, uh, I guess I’m here because things have gotten a bit out of hand lately. You see, I work at this big family entertainment center—arcade games, laser tag, go-karts, the whole nine yards. It’s loud, it’s chaotic, and I usually get stuck on the closing shifts, which means I’m not walking out of there until way past midnight most nights. By the time I leave, I’m just completely drained, physically and mentally. So, I have this habit, or routine I guess, where I’ll stop and grab some food on the way back to my apartment. At first, it was just, you know, a normal late-night dinner because I was starving. But lately, it’s like... I can’t stop once I start. I’ll get a massive takeout meal, like a huge burger and fries, maybe some nuggets, and I’ll eat all of that in the car or as soon as I walk in the door. But then, instead of feeling full or going to bed, I just keep going. I’ll open the pantry and tear through a family-sized bag of chips, then I’ll move on to sweets—cookies, ice cream, literally whatever I can find in the kitchen. It’s like I’m on autopilot or something. I just keep eating and eating until there’s nothing left or until my stomach physically hurts. And then, when I finally snap out of it and look at all the empty wrappers and containers scattered around, I’m just... I’m honestly shocked. I look at it all and think, "How did one person eat all of this?" It’s really starting to scare me, honestly, because I just feel so out of control when it happens, and it’s happening more and more after those late shifts.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you’ve eaten?

Well, yeah, actually... that’s the other part of it that I’ve been really struggling to admit. After I eat all that food—like, when I’m standing there looking at the wrappers and feeling just this intense wave of guilt and panic—I start thinking about all those calories. I mean, at 40, your metabolism just isn't what it used to be, right? So I’ll be standing in my kitchen, my stomach stretched tight and hurting, and I just get this overwhelming fear that all that food is just going to sit in me and turn straight into weight. It’s terrifying, honestly. 

So, um, sometimes... well, more often lately after those really bad nights... I’ll go into the bathroom. I’ll turn on the fan or run the water so my neighbors don't hear, even though I know they probably can't anyway, but my mind just races. And then I’ll, you know, make myself throw up. I’ll just lean over the toilet and force it all out. It’s awful, it really is. My throat burns, my eyes water, and I feel so ashamed afterward, wiping my face with a towel and looking at myself in the mirror. I never thought I’d be a guy who does something like that, but in the moment, it feels like the only way to undo the damage, to just get it out of my system before it has a chance to stick to my ribs. I don't use laxatives or go run a marathon or anything—I'm way too exhausted from the arcade for that—but the throwing up... yeah, that’s what I do. It just feels like I have to hit a reset button, even though I know it's messed up.
How often do these episodes of overeating followed by making yourself vomit happen? Are they happening at least once a week, and have they been going on for more than three months?

Well, um, let me think about the timeline here. It really started picking up after I moved into this new apartment. The move itself was a huge hassle, you know? Packing up all my stuff, dealing with the leasing office, trying to figure out where to put everything in a smaller space... it was just a lot of stress on top of the crazy hours at the arcade. But once I finally got settled in and things kind of fell into a routine—or, I guess, a bad routine—that’s when this whole cycle really took hold. 

So, since the move settled down, I'd say most weeks I have at least one of these late-night episodes. You know, where I just eat way, way past what I meant to, tearing through all those wrappers like I mentioned. And then, because I just can't stand the thought of all those calories sitting there, I try to make up for it. Sometimes it's the throwing up, like I said, which is just awful. But other times, if I can't bring myself to do that, I'll wake up the next day and just completely skip breakfast, maybe even lunch, just drinking black coffee to keep my stomach empty. Or, if I have a day off and I'm feeling especially guilty, I'll force myself to go on this incredibly long, punishing run, even though my knees ache and I hate running. I just feel like I have to burn it off somehow. 

As for how long this has been going on... yeah, it's definitely been more than three months. The move was back in the spring, so it’s been a solid four or five months now of this happening pretty much every week. It just feels like this awful loop I’m stuck in, you know? Like, I tell myself every Monday that this week will be different, that I'll just come home, have a normal sandwich, and go to bed. But then Thursday rolls around, the arcade is a madhouse with a kids' birthday party, I'm exhausted, and before I know it, I'm back in the drive-thru line, starting the whole thing over again. It's just... it's exhausting, honestly.
Do you only make yourself vomit or skip meals and exercise after these late-night overeating episodes, or do you ever do these things even when you haven't overeaten?

Well, um, that's an interesting question. I guess... I mean, I really only do all that stuff—the throwing up, the starving myself the next day, or pushing myself to run until my legs feel like jelly—after I've had one of those massive binges. It's really tied to that specific feeling, you know? Like, if I just come home and manage to eat a normal meal, say, a bowl of soup and half a sandwich, I don't feel that overwhelming, crushing panic. I might still worry about my weight, sure, because, like I said, hitting 40 really changes your perspective on how your body handles things. You start noticing every little change, how your jeans fit a little tighter after a holiday weekend, or how you get winded just carrying groceries up the stairs to the apartment. But I don't go into the bathroom and turn on the fan unless I've completely lost it and eaten the burgers, the fries, the chips, the cookies... all of it. 

It's the sheer volume of the food that triggers it. When I haven't overeaten, I don't feel that desperate need to hit the reset button. I mean, sure, there are days when I might skip breakfast just because I overslept after a late shift, but that's different. That's just me rushing out the door, grabbing my keys, and realizing I don't have time to make toast. It's not this calculated, punishing thing where I'm denying myself food to make up for a mistake. The throwing up and the intense exercise, those are definitely reactions to the big episodes. It's like a direct cause and effect. I eat all that food, I feel the guilt and the physical discomfort of being so full, and then I do whatever I can to undo it. If the binge doesn't happen, the purge—or whatever you want to call it—doesn't happen either. It's all just connected to those late nights when I lose control.
